arxiv-2011-00921.title: Two-Meson Form Factors in Unitarized Chiral Perturbation Theory
arxiv-2011-00921.creator: Yu-Ji Shi, Chien-Yeah Seng, Feng-Kun Guo, Bastian Kubis, Ulf-G. Meißner, and Wei Wang
arxiv-2011-00921.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yu-Ji Shi, Chien-Yeah Seng, Feng-Kun Guo, Bastian Kubis, Ulf-G. Meißner, and Wei Wang. We present a comprehensive analysis of form factors for two light pseudoscalar mesons induced by scalar, vector, and tensor quark operators. The theoretical framework is based on a combination of unitarized chiral perturbation theory and dispersion relations. The low-energy constants in chiral perturbation theory are fixed by a global fit to the available data of the two-meson scattering phase shifts.

arxiv-2202-01072.title: Interpretability for Multimodal Emotion Recognition using Concept Activation Vectors
arxiv-2202-01072.creator: Ashish Ramayee Asokan, Nidarshan Kumar, Anirudh V Ragam, Shylaja S S
arxiv-2202-01072.description: Abstract Multimodal Emotion Recognition refers to the classification of input video sequences into emotion labels based on multiple input modalities (usually video, audio and text). In recent years, Deep Neural networks have shown remarkable performance in recognizing human emotions, and are on par with human-level performance on this task.

arxiv-2208-10119.title: Predicting the Biological Classification of Cell-Cycle Regulated Genes of Saccharomyces cerevisiae using Community Detection Algorithms on Gene Co-expression Networks
arxiv-2208-10119.creator: Jhoirene Clemente, Gabriel Besas, Jerick Callado, and John Erol Evangelista
arxiv-2208-10119.description: Abstract . The conventional approach for analyzing gene expression data involves clustering algorithms. Cluster analyses provide partitioning of the set of genes that can predict biological classification based on its similarity in n n -dimensional space. In this study, we investigate whether network analysis will provide an advantage over the traditional approach.

arxiv-2303-04394.title: Analytic continuation of the relativistic three-particle scattering amplitudes
arxiv-2303-04394.creator: Sebastian M. Dawid, Md Habib E Islam, Raúl A. Briceño
arxiv-2303-04394.description: Abstract We investigate the relativistic scattering of three identical scalar bosons interacting via pair-wise interactions. Extending techniques from the non-relativistic three-body scattering theory, we provide a detailed and general prescription for solving and analytically continuing integral equations describing the three-body reactions.

arxiv-2310-00541.title: Robust Nonparametric Hypothesis Testing to Understand Variability in Training Neural Networks
arxiv-2310-00541.creator: Sinjini Banerjee, Reilly Cannon, Tim Marrinan, Tony Chiang, Anand D. Sarwate
arxiv-2310-00541.description: Abstract Training a deep neural network (DNN) often involves stochastic optimization, which means each run will produce a different model. Several works suggest this variability is negligible when models have the same performance, which in the case of classification is test accuracy. However, models with similar test accuracy may not be computing the same function.

arxiv-2312-04936.title: SKT-Hang: Hanging Everyday Objects via Object-Agnostic Semantic Keypoint Trajectory Generation
arxiv-2312-04936.creator: Chia-Liang Kuo Yu-Wei Chao Yi-Ting Chen
arxiv-2312-04936.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chia-Liang Kuo Yu-Wei Chao Yi-Ting Chen. We study the problem of hanging a wide range of grasped objects on diverse supporting items. Hanging objects is a ubiquitous task that is encountered in numerous aspects of our everyday lives.

arxiv-2404-02262.title: Classification and Regression Error Bounds for Inhomogenous Data With Applications to Wireless Networks
arxiv-2404-02262.creator: Ghurumuruhan Ganesan
arxiv-2404-02262.description: Abstract In this paper, we study classification and regression error bounds for inhomogenous data that are independent but not necessarily identically distributed. First, we consider classification of data in the presence of non-stationary noise and establish ergodic type sufficient conditions that guarantee the achievability of the Bayes error bound, using universal rules.

arxiv-2404-07197.title: An Indeterminacy-based Ontology for Quantum Theory
arxiv-2404-07197.creator: Francisco Pipa
arxiv-2404-07197.description: Abstract I present and defend a new ontology for quantum theories (or “interpretations” of quantum theory) called Generative Quantum Theory (GQT). GQT postulates different sets of features, and the combination of these different features can help generate different quantum theories.

arxiv-2511-02791.title: AI-Generated Image Detection: An Empirical Study and Future Research Directions
arxiv-2511-02791.creator: Nusrat Tasnim, Kutub Uddin, Khalid Mahmood Malik
arxiv-2511-02791.description: Abstract The threats posed by AI-generated media, particularly deepfakes, are now raising significant challenges for multimedia forensics, misinformation detection, and biometric system resulting in erosion of public trust in the legal system, significant increase in frauds, and social engineering attacks.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-codex-sinaiti.creator: John Francis Fenlon
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-codex-sinaiti.description: Article 'Codex Sinaiticus' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-10497570.title: Single nucleus transcriptomics of ventral midbrain identifies glial activation associated with chronic opioid use disorder
pmc-10497570.creator: Julong Wei, Tova Y. Lambert, Aditi Valada, Nikhil Patel, Kellie Walker, Jayna Lenders, Carl J. Schmidt, Marina Iskhakova, Adnan Alazizi, Henriette Mair-Meijers, Deborah C. Mash, Francesca Luca, Roger Pique-Regi, Michael J. Bannon, Schahram Akbarian
pmc-10497570.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Dynamic interactions of neurons and glia in the ventral midbrain mediate reward and addiction behavior. We studied gene expression in 212,713 ventral midbrain single nuclei from 95 individuals with history of opioid misuse, and individuals without drug exposure. Chronic exposure to opioids was not associated with change in proportions of glial and neuronal subtypes, however glial transcriptomes were broadly altered, involving 9.5 − 6.2% of expressed genes within microglia, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes.

pmc-10688998.title: Reducing the risks of nuclear war: the role of health professionals†
pmc-10688998.creator: Andy Haines, Ira Helfand, Arun Mitra, Tilman Ruff, Chris Zielinski, Kamran Abbasi, Parveen Ali, Virginia Barbour, Kirsten Bibbins-Domingo, Marcel G M Olde Rikkert, Peng Gong, Richard Horton, Bob Mash, Carlos Monteiro, Elena N Naumova, Eric J Rubin, Peush Sahni, James Tumwine, Paul Yonga
pmc-10688998.description: day Clock forward to 90 s before midnight, reflecting the growing risk of nuclear war.1 In August 2022, the UN Secretary-General, António Guterres warned that the world is now in ‘a time of nuclear danger not seen since the height of the Cold War’.2 The danger has been underlined by growing tensions between many nuclear armed states.

pmc-11354399.title: Increased Pan-Type, A1-Type, and A2-Type Astrocyte Activation and Upstream Inflammatory Markers Are Induced by the P2X7 Receptor
pmc-11354399.creator: Keith E Campagno, Puttipong Sripinun, Lily P See, Jiaqi Li, Wennan Lu, Assraa Hassan Jassim, Néstor Más Gómez, Claire H Mitchell, Hiroshi Tomita
pmc-11354399.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study asked whether the P2X7 receptor was necessary and sufficient to trigger astrocyte polarization into neuroinflammatory activation states. Intravitreal injection of agonist BzATP increased gene expression of pan-astrocyte activation markers Gfap, Steap4, and Vim and A1-type astrocyte activation markers C3, Serping1, and H2T23, but also the Cd14 and Ptx3 genes usually associated with the A2-type astrocyte activation state and Tnfa, IL1a, and C1qa, assumed to be upstream of astrocyte activation in microglia.

pmc-11432376.title: A Longitudinal Decline in Walking Speed Is Linked with Coexisting Hypertension and Arthritis in Community-Dwelling Older Adults
pmc-11432376.creator: Saud M Alrawaili, Khalid Alkhathami, Mohammed G Elsehrawy, Mohammed S Alghamdi, Hussein M Alkahtani, Norah A Alhwoaimel, Aqeel M Alenazi, Rubén Cuesta-Barriuso
pmc-11432376.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective: The aim was to investigate the association between baseline coexistence of hypertension (HTN) and arthritis, HTN alone, or arthritis alone, and their impact on longitudinal physical function measures among community-dwelling older adults over 5 years of follow-up. Methods: Ours was a longitudinal prospective cohort study from the second wave (2010–2011) and third wave (2015–2016) of the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (NSHAP). Data for older adults were used.

pmc-12365051.title: Dynamics of 4D supply chain system with fractal fractional derivatives insight of stability analysis and ANN prediction
pmc-12365051.creator: Anum Zehra, Muhammad Farman, Talal Bonny, Aceng Sambas, Wafaa Al Nassan, Kottakkaran Sooppy Nisar, Betty Wan Niu Voon, Mohamed Hafez
pmc-12365051.description: This paper investigated 4D supply chain finance system utilizing fractal fractional derivatives with the generalized Mittag-Leffler kernel. The model incorporates key interactions between customer demand, distributor inventory, and retailer orders, creating a dynamic system governed by fractional-order differential equations. We analyze the positiveness and boundedness of the systems solutions.

pmc-12418612.title: Long-term recovery of sensorimotor functions and prediction of participation in survivors of critical illness: a prospective cohort study
pmc-12418612.creator: Johanna Weghorn, Melanie Finsterhölzl, Franziska Wippenbeck, Klaus Jahn, Marion Egger, Jeannine Bergmann
pmc-12418612.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSurvivors of critical illness frequently face physical, cognitive and psychological impairments after intensive care. Sensorimotor impairments potentially have a negative impact on participation. However, comprehensive understanding of sensorimotor recovery and participation in survivors of critical illness is limited.

pmc-12612146.title: Sleep quality and body composition in active and inactive young adults
pmc-12612146.creator: Krystian Maruszczak, Wojciech Kasperek, Konrad Kustra, Grzegorz Przysada, Maciej Kochman
pmc-12612146.description: Body composition is influenced by a variety of internal and external factors, with early adulthood being a particularly sensitive period for its fluctuations. This observational study aimed to assess the differences in body composition, anthropometric indices, and sleep quality between active and inactive young adults as well as to explore the relationship between these parameters.

pmc-12625269.title: Pregnancy and postpartum-related admissions to the intensive care unit at a tertiary centre in Northwest China: a 14-year retrospective study
pmc-12625269.creator: Weiwei Yuan, Yanni Zheng, Xu Zhang, Tingting Li, Haiwang Sha, Zhiyan Hui
pmc-12625269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe purpose of this study was to analyse the incidence of maternal morbidity and mortality of pregnant and postpartum women admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsIn this study, we retrospectively analyzed all pregnant and postpartum patients admitted to the ICU of the intensive care unit at our tertiary center in northwest China between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2022.ResultsA total of 528 patients with pregnancy and postpartum related morbidities were admitted to the ICU (5.16 per 1000 deliveries).

pmc-12980470.title: Designed Water Capture in Terpene Synthase Catalysis
pmc-12980470.creator: Prabhakar L. Srivastava, David J. Miller, Rudolf K. Allemann
pmc-12980470.description: Sesquiterpene synthases catalyse cyclisations and rearrangements of farnesyl diphosphate to produce a diverse array of sesquiterpenes generated by depronotation and/or water capture. However, the precise mechanisms and dynamics controlling the fate of the final carbocationic intermediate are not well understood.

pmc-13311372.title: Multimodal Transformer Fusion of PTR‐ToF‐MS Volatiles and Targeted Non‐Volatile Metabolites Enables Data‐Driven Grading of Baimudan White Tea
pmc-13311372.creator: Dandan Zhang, Suk‐Hwan Hong, Xiaojing Li
pmc-13311372.description: RationaleCommercial grading of Baimudan white tea still relies largely on sensory evaluation and would benefit from a rapid, objective analytical approach. This study investigated whether PTR‐ToF‐MS volatile fingerprints combined with targeted non‐volatile metabolite measurements could support data‐driven grading of four official Baimudan grades.

pmc-13669228.title: Interface Rectification via Roll‐to‐Roll Dual‐Confinement Nanocoatings for High‐Temperature Polymer Capacitors
pmc-13669228.creator: Ning Guo, Marina Dabaghian, Jierui Zhou, Josh N. Bodin, Chong Xiang, Fei Wang, Antigoni Konstantinou, Dingxin Wei, Yifei Wang, Chao Wu, Riccardo Casalini, Bryan Huey, Priya Vashishta, Luyi Sun, Yang Cao
pmc-13669228.description: Polymer film capacitors are indispensable for energy storage and power conversion, yet their energy density and efficiency deteriorate rapidly at elevated temperatures. At temperatures relevant to wide‐bandgap semiconductor electronics (>150°C), heat‐resistant polymer films must be heavily derated to avoid premature aging due to intensive hot‐carrier injection.

pmc-13677807.title: Efficacy and safety of pharmacological interventions for the treatment of cocaine use disorder: A systematic review and network meta‐analysis
pmc-13677807.creator: Craig Paterson, Thomas Parkhouse, Chloe Burke, Monika Halicka, Jennifer C. Palmer, Hend Gabr, Rebecca Wilson, Katie E. Webster, Francesca Spiga, Sarah Dawson, Deborah M. Caldwell, Jennifer Scott, Julian P. T. Higgins, Jelena Savović
pmc-13677807.description: Background and aimsCocaine use disorder (CUD) is an increasingly widespread concern worldwide. Various pharmacological treatments have been investigated for CUD, but their efficacy remains unclear, and none have been licensed for treatment. Therefore, we assessed the comparative effectiveness, safety and acceptability of pharmacological interventions for the treatment of CUD and prevention of relapse.
